overview: This 115-page file traces Japan’s zinc, iron, and steel industries from 1932 to 1939, emphasizing imported ore and American scrap. Its correspondence follows proposals to move an Ohio steel machinery plant to Japan and supply steel on credit, alongside debates over export controls, neutrality, and public objections.
interest: The file links industrial statistics to U.S. policy debates and public resistance to supplying Japan during its war in China.
